claims.claim: Wolfe says a writer develops his own voice but keeps some imprint of the writers who impressed him young.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe interviewed by Neil Gaiman, Locus 500, September 2002
claims.quote: you always bear some imprint of the people

claims.claim: Wolfe says that as long as a writer sticks to explaining he will have an explanatory lump somewhere in the story.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe interviewed by Robert Frazier, Thrust 19, Winter/Spring 1983
claims.quote: As long as you stick to explaining, you're going to

claims.claim: Wolfe attributes the New Sun books' visual clarity to Severian's straightforwardness as against his earlier narrators.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe interviewed by Robert Frazier, Thrust 19, Winter/Spring 1983
claims.quote: Severian's straightforwardness, as opposed to someone like Number Five

claims.claim: Asked whether any of the archaic terms in The Book of the New Sun were invented, Wolfe answered that none were.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe interviewed by Robert Frazier, Thrust 19, Winter/Spring 1983
claims.quote: None. Some of the terms are Latin

claims.claim: Wolfe says the stories inside The Book of the New Sun shed light on the world in which the action takes place.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe interviewed by Robert Frazier, Thrust 19, Winter/Spring 1983
claims.quote: They shed light on the world in which the action

claims.claim: Wolfe says the inset stories act as dividers between parts of the action that should be divided.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe interviewed by Robert Frazier, Thrust 19, Winter/Spring 1983
claims.quote: They act as dividers between parts of the action

claims.claim: Asked to describe Severian, Wolfe answered with a flat physical inventory giving his height as 6'1" and his weight as 175 pounds.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe interviewed by Robert Frazier, Thrust 19, Winter/Spring 1983
claims.quote: He is pale, with dark eyes, dark straight hair

claims.claim: Wolfe says the best surprises grow from the material of the story itself when the writer faces its consequences.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe interviewed by Robert Frazier, Thrust 19, Winter/Spring 1983
claims.quote: growing from the material of the story itself

claims.claim: Wolfe contrasts the forms photographically, calling short stories stills and novellas and novels movies.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe interviewed by Robert Frazier, Thrust 19, Winter/Spring 1983
claims.quote: short stories are stills; novellas and novels are movies

claims.claim: Wolfe mentions having been an army cartographer in Korea after the cease-fire.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe interviewed by Robert Frazier, Thrust 19, Winter/Spring 1983
claims.quote: I was an army cartographer in Korea

claims.claim: Wolfe calls a line of dialogue wasted unless it is said in some particular way or serves the character's purpose.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, Locus 'Engineering the Future' excerpts, 20 March 2011
claims.quote: it's a waste unless it's said in some particular way

claims.claim: Wolfe lists the simultaneous jobs of a passage as tone, plot movement and character.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, Locus 'Engineering the Future' excerpts, 20 March 2011
claims.quote: pique the tone of the book; to move the plot forward

claims.claim: Wolfe says that in his first year of writing he wasted such scenes and later cut them.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, Locus 'Engineering the Future' excerpts, 20 March 2011
claims.quote: I used to waste that kind of scene

claims.claim: Wolfe says that if he is not having fun the reader will not have fun either.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, Locus 'Engineering the Future' excerpts, 20 March 2011
claims.quote: If I'm not having fun, it's not going to be
